chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: Playing at King Farouk's wedding and leaving for Holland
summary: Before summer the band left Egypt for Holland, having played King Farouk's wedding, and Chittison nearly got jailed again; Wilson Miles was passing himself off as a local.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So we stayed there, but we had to leave. It was -- summertime was coming on, we had to go to Holland so Burns and Pastotis were looking at each other and Pastotis was getting eviler every day, so Burns wanted to stay there, but he says, I'll come back. We take off and get our business straight and change -- Egyptian pounds, when you change an Egyptian pound, at the Barclay's Express or the Cook's, you got so much money, and you had gold, and in the meantime we played for King Farouk's wedding. He became the king of Egypt because his uncle had died.

I didn't know that they were Turks but Farouk was a Turk, he wasn't Egyptian and we played for his wedding and I saw all those people and one of them looked like my aunt and she was just happy as she could be, the things that we were doing. In fact, we were the beloved, but Chitteson he almost got put in that thing again. They hesitated to let Chitteson go.

Now, we had another boy named Wilson Miles, well, they swear that he was from there, and Wilson Miles was there about two weeks and he was on the corner talking to the cabdrivers. He was just talking as if he were a citizen of the place, so all right, we all got our pay and got all our money
